name: Emface

lead: Emface combines radiofrequency heating of the skin with electrical stimulation of facial muscles. It is used for smoother wrinkles, firmer muscle tone and a lifted look without needles.

RF energy heats the dermis to stimulate collagen remodelling, while stimulation makes the facial muscles contract. Headline figures such as 37% wrinkle improvement come from manufacturer-linked data; no independent peer-reviewed trial was found.

paras: It is typically a course of four sessions of about 20 minutes each in a clinic, with no needles or downtime.
No Emface-specific safety data were found. A 2025 study of non-surgical aesthetic treatments generally reports that complications are underreported.

trials.title: EMVITAL + EMFACE Combination Therapy for Temporomandibular Joint (TMJ) Pain Relief

chain: RF heats skin, stimulates facial muscles
angle.text: It is used as a needle-free way to smooth wrinkles and lift the face over a short course of sessions. RF heat builds collagen while muscle stimulation firms tone, giving a lifted, smoother face. The headline improvement figures come mainly from manufacturer-supported data.

lead: Emface is a facial treatment from BTL Aesthetics that applies radiofrequency (RF) energy to the skin together with high-intensity facial electrical stimulation (HIFES) of facial muscles, marketed for wrinkle reduction, muscle tone and a lifting effect without needles.[1] It is typically described as a four-session course of about 20 minutes each.[1]

The figures commonly quoted for it, such as 37% wrinkle improvement, come from manufacturer-linked data repeated in an AI-generated encyclopedia entry.[1] No independent peer-reviewed trial of Emface was found among the sources for this article.

paras: The RF component heats the dermis to stimulate collagen remodeling, while HIFES induces contractions in facial muscles, particularly the cheeks.[1] It is applied to the cheeks, jawline, eyebrows and forehead, and a separate submental applicator targets the area under the chin.[1] The device is described as FDA-cleared for facial wrinkles.[1]

The manufacturer-derived figures are a 37% wrinkle reduction, 23% higher facial muscle tone and 26% improvement in lift, and, for the submental applicator, a 30.37% reduction in submental fat volume on MRI at three months.[1] These are manufacturer-linked claims and the source may contain errors.

No independent published trials were found. A registered trial started in December 2025 combines Emface with another BTL device for temporomandibular joint pain, a medical rather than appearance use.[2] A broad 2025 mixed-methods study of non-surgical aesthetic treatment complications reports that complications are underreported and inconsistently regulated across the category, without being specific to Emface.[3]
